Dalunde (Verts/ALE), Alice Kuhnke (Verts/ALE), Pär Holmgren (Verts/ALE), Dimitrios Papadimoulis (The Left), Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Rosa D'Amato (Verts/ALE), Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Silvia Modig (The Left), Idoia Villanueva Ruiz (The Left), Margrete Auken (Verts/ALE), Barry Andrews (Renew), Piernicola Pedicini (Verts/ALE), Francisco Guerreiro (Verts/ALE), Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Kateřina Konečná (The Left), María Soraya Rodríguez Ramos (Renew), Maria Arena (S&D), Chris MacManus (The Left), Karen Melchior (Renew), José Gusmão (The Left), Marisa Matias (The Left), Luke Ming Flanagan (The Left), Ville Niinistö (Verts/ALE), Ciarán Cuffe (Verts/ALE), Malin Björk (The Left), Heidi Hautala (Verts/ALE), François Alfonsi (Verts/ALE), Marc Botenga (The Left), Pierre Larrouturou (S&D) Subject:

On Friday 26 January 2024, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ordered Israel to take all measures within its power to prevent death, destruction and acts of genocide in its siege of over 2 million people in Gaza, which has seen almost 30 000 people killed, mostly women and children, in relentless airstrikes and ground assaults. In a statement, the Commission and the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy underlined that the parties must comply with the provisional orders of the ICJ. And yet in the 72 hours following the ruling, Israel has killed over 500 Palestinians and has continued to target civilian infrastructure, including hospitals. In addition, Israeli government ministers and lawmakers attended a conference on 28 January where they openly called for the illegal settlement and ethnic cleansing of Gaza. In short, the Israeli Government has completely disregarded the ruling of the ICJ. 1.
How will the Commission respond to Israel’s immediate breaches of the provisional orders of the ICJ?

How does the Commission justify the fact that the EU-Israel Association Agreement is still in force given the breaches of Article 2, which stipulates that relations ‘shall be based on respect for human rights’?

2. How does the Commission justify the fact that the EU-Israel Association Agreement is still in force given the breaches of Article 2, which stipulates that relations ‘shall be based on respect for human rights’? (30 April 2024) The EU continues to urge all sides to respect international law and notes that there must be accountability for violations of international law. The EU consistently underlines the importance of ensuring the protection of all civilians at all times in line with international humanitarian law. As stated in the joint statement by the High Representative/Vice-President and the Commission on 26 January 2024, orders of the International Court of Justice are binding on the Parties and they must comply with them. The EU expects their full, immediate and effective implementation (1). The Foreign Affairs Council had an orientation debate on 18 March 2024 regarding the question of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, which is based on shared values, including the respect for human rights. The Council agreed to continue following this question closely and to invite the Foreign Minister of Israel for a discussion on this matter.
